data.content_ref: inline:The target's defense relies on the premise that acting on the 'unrefuted' theory is the 'only non-irrational choice,' but this smuggles in induction by implicitly assuming that past survival (corroboration) is a reliable indicator of future utility or truth-likeness. If corroboration provides no probabilistic weight regarding future performance, as Popper insists, then preferring Theory A (highly corroborated) over Theory B (newly conjectured and untested) for practical action is logically arbitrary within his own framework. The target fails to explain why 'past severe testing' confers any rational priority for 'future action' without invoking the very inductive principle (that the future will resemble the past) that Popper explicitly rejected. Thus, the preference is not defensible on his own terms without contradiction.
